true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The second downsize definition replaces the existing API

Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` method. Existing callers supplying width, height, and options will now raise ArgumentError. Callers supplying only width and height will bind the height to `opts`, then fail when optimization accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve both calling conventions in a single method or give the dimensions-string variant a separate name.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Large animated GIFs lose their animation even when it is allowed

The new downsizing call passes the upload's temporary path rather than its original filename. `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects animated processing only when the source path ends in `.gif`, but multipart upload tempfiles normally have no such extension. Consequently, even with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, a large animated GIF is processed by the static ImageMagick instructions, which read only frame `[0]`. Because this operation overwrites the upload itself, the animation is permanently discarded before storage. Detect the image format independently of the tempfile extension or use a correctly suffixed temporary file.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are not normalized for the new lookup

The migration inserts old embeddable_hosts entries verbatim, bypassing the new model's normalization callback. The previous host check accepted entries such as http://eviltrout.com and https://eviltrout.com, but the new lookup compares the stored value directly with URI.host, which is only eviltrout.com. Those previously working configurations stop allowing embeds after upgrade, and the original settings are deleted. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the new lookup.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when no embed category is configured

The category query can return no rows when embed_category is unset (its default is an empty string) or names a deleted category. Indexing [0]['id'] then dereferences nil before the uncategorized fallback is reached. This prevents migrations from completing on ordinary installations that have never configured embedding. Handle an empty result before accessing the row.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

false_positives.candidate:
Host validation rejects valid longer top-level domains

The new format validation restricts the final domain label to two through five letters. Valid hosts such as example.museum or example.technology therefore cannot be added or saved in the embedding editor, although the previous host setting and lookup had no such restriction. Use hostname validation that supports valid longer top-level domains.

Hosts saved with ports can never match incoming URLs

The host validator accepts values such as example.com:8080 and the normalization callback preserves the port, but record_for_host compares that value against uri.host, which excludes the port. Thus a host successfully added as example.com:8080 will reject even http://example.com:8080 and will not supply its configured category to imports. Make storage and lookup agree on how ports are handled.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when the current user has no TopicUser record

TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a visible topic the current user has never visited. This can happen when an email link is opened while logged into a different account or when a forwarded link is opened. The action then dereferences tu.notification_level and returns a server error instead of handling the unsubscribe. Resolve the default notification level and create the user's preference record when none exists.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Client-side entry never performs the unsubscribe operation

The Ember unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view through PostStream.loadTopicView; it never calls the unsubscribe endpoint or changes the notification level. When this URL is entered through client-side navigation, the Rails HTML GET action does not run, yet the template tells the user they will stop receiving notifications. Ensure this flow explicitly performs the preference change rather than relying on an initial full-page server request.

Direct save allows automatic tracking to undo unsubscribe

The unsubscribe action updates notification_level directly and saves the TopicUser without setting notifications_reason_id. For users whose topic tracking was automatic and whose reason is still nil, TopicUser.update_last_read explicitly restores tracking once the reading-time threshold is exceeded. Consequently, reading the topic after unsubscribing can undo this explicit preference. Use TopicUser.change, as set_notifications does, so the user_changed reason and notification-change metadata are recorded.

Notification preferences are mutated by an unprotected GET request

The new GET unsubscribe route immediately saves notification preferences for the session's current user, without a recipient token or a POST confirmation. Rails CSRF protection does not protect GET requests, so another site can navigate a logged-in user to this URL and silently downgrade or mute notifications for a topic. Keep GET read-only and perform the change through a CSRF-protected request (or an appropriately validated recipient-specific unsubscribe token).

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrent matches lose counter increments

The match counter is updated using a read-modify-save sequence without locking. Two simultaneous checks for the same blocked email can both read the same match_count and save the same incremented value, recording only one match instead of two. Use an atomic database increment or a locked update to preserve the statistics under concurrent registration attempts.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Case-sensitive lookup allows blocked addresses to register

BlockedEmail looks up the supplied email with an exact, case-sensitive equality comparison, and neither this model nor User.new_from_params normalizes it. A block for `block@example.com` therefore does not stop registration with `block@EXAMPLE.COM`, even though the domain refers to the same mailbox. Normalize addresses consistently when storing blocked entries and checking user emails so casing cannot bypass the block.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed imports persist unsanitized HTML as cooked posts

Imported contents are parsed by Nokogiri but never sanitized before being saved with the raw_html cook method, which returns the HTML unchanged. PollFeed passes feed content directly into this method, so script tags, event-handler attributes, and dangerous links from a feed become stored executable content on the forum's origin. The source URL is also interpolated into HTML without escaping. Sanitize the final imported HTML, including the attribution link, before bypassing the cooking pipeline.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid Ruby prevents the discussion template from rendering

The conditional is closed with `end if` rather than `end`. The trailing `if` has no condition, so the generated ERB Ruby fails to compile. Every embed request that finds an existing topic will fail instead of displaying the discussion. Close the block with `end` and add a test that renders the actual view.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
RSS entries without a content element abort feed polling

The poller unconditionally calls `scrub` on `i.content`. Valid RSS feeds commonly provide article text in `description` rather than a content element; for those entries, content is nil and polling raises instead of importing the entry. Since the exception exits the loop and retries are disabled, later entries also go unprocessed. Handle missing content and use the appropriate RSS description fallback.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Relative URL conversion corrupts protocol-relative links

The URL conversion treats every href beginning with `/` as a path on the article host. A valid protocol-relative link such as `//cdn.example.com/file` is consequently rewritten to `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/file`; the image conversion below has the same problem. Path-relative links such as `images/photo.jpg` are not resolved at all and instead point at the forum when rendered there. Resolve references against the full source URI rather than concatenating the source host.

Remote retrieval follows redirects outside the allowed embed host

TopicRetriever validates only the initial URL's host, then this method fetches it with open-uri, which follows HTTP redirects. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host can therefore cause the worker to fetch internal HTTP services and publish their extracted content as a topic, bypassing the embedding host restriction. Validate redirect destinations and resolved addresses before each request, rejecting private or otherwise disallowed targets.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Apply the website visibility restriction to website_name

The new website_name attribute is not included in untrusted_attributes, and include_website_name lacks the trailing '?' required for a serializer inclusion predicate. Consequently, an anonymous viewer of a TL0 user receives the website hostname (and, for matching domains, its path) even when scope.restrict_user_fields? suppresses website. The template also displays this leaked value because it now checks website_name independently. Apply the same restriction as website and add a test with a populated TL0 website.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

Exact multiples of the page size produce an empty extra page

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Existing membership PATCH requests silently hide groups

The resources route still accepts PATCH /admin/groups/:id, but update no longer handles the previously supported changes: {add: ... , delete: ...} payload. Such a request now ignores the membership changes and sets visible to false because it contains no visible parameter, then returns success. Existing API clients therefore silently lose their membership updates and unintentionally hide the group. Preserve the PATCH contract or explicitly reject unsupported payloads without modifying the group.

Public member lists are truncated without a way to load subsequent pages

The shared findMembers method now requests only 50 members, and the server applies that limit to all groups. This public route fetches only once, while the public group/members template has no pagination or load-more controls. Consequently, members beyond the first 50 are inaccessible on the public group page; previously nonautomatic groups returned their complete membership. Add pagination to the public page alongside the new paginated response.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Include the site fallback locale in translation cache identity

The fallback result now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator caches no-argument translations using only the key, current locale, and backend object ID. If a key is missing in the user's locale, its site-language fallback is cached and remains in use after the administrator changes the site's default locale. Include the fallback configuration in the cache key or invalidate the cache when it changes; otherwise users continue receiving translations from the old fallback language.

Load fallback locales for translations outside controller requests

Fallback locales are only preloaded by ApplicationController#set_locale. The translation wrapper still loads only config.locale, and the patched backend disables automatic loading. In a background worker or mailer that has not processed a controller request, translating a missing key in a non-English locale therefore cannot find the site-locale or English translation unless those locales happen to have been loaded previously. Load the fallback chain in the translation path, rather than relying on a controller callback, so server-side fallbacks also work for jobs and mail.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Call to conditional-passkey helper does not compile

UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without arguments, but the only method defined in its superclass is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). There is no zero-argument overload in the supplied inheritance chain, so the services module fails compilation. Pass the context user or provide an appropriate overload.

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Conditional passkeys are disabled for ordinary unidentified logins

The new helper requires user != null, and both initial form rendering and error challenges now use it. During an ordinary login context.getUser() is null, so fillContextForm() is no longer called and the login page receives neither conditional WebAuthn UI attributes nor a WebAuthn challenge. This removes the existing username-less passkey login path (including for passkey-only users) and breaks the existing discoverable-key login tests. true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Django querysets do not support the advertised negative-offset slicing

When advanced features are enabled and a cursor has a negative offset (for example, 0:-1:0), this branch passes that offset directly to QuerySet slicing. Django explicitly rejects negative slice indices with ValueError; it does not handle these boundary conditions automatically as the comment claims. Thus the new negative-offset feature produces a server error rather than reverse pagination. Translate offsets into supported nonnegative queries or reject them with a pagination validation error before slicing.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log datetime values

OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so get_item_key receives a datetime object. math.floor/math.ceil cannot convert a datetime and raise TypeError when build_cursor processes any nonempty result set. Consequently, eligible users requesting optimized_pagination=true get a server error instead of audit logs. The cursor conversion also returns a raw number rather than a datetime for subsequent queries. Use the DateTimePaginator key encoding and decoding for this endpoint.

false_positives.candidate:
Changing existing Redis set keys to sorted sets requires a migration

The buffer now issues ZADD and ZSCAN against the same span-buf:s:* keys that the previous implementation populated with SADD. Existing buffered segments remain Redis sets, so new ingestion into those keys and flushing them will fail with WRONGTYPE after deployment. Mixed-version consumers also cannot read each other's buffers. Introduce a versioned key namespace with a drain strategy, or explicitly migrate/drain existing keys before switching commands, to avoid blocking processing and losing buffered segments.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use the dataset and query actually being executed for eligibility

The eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` and the original request query instead of `scoped_dataset` and the `query` passed to this invocation. The dashboard-splitting path explicitly calls this function with Discover and an errors-only query while the outer dataset is metrics-enhanced performance. The helper rejects that outer dataset, so counts for sampled error events remain unweighted in those dashboard results, including widgets already classified as error events. Base eligibility on the scoped execution context so these error queries receive the same upsampling as direct error queries.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Substring matching does not establish an errors-only query

The presence of `event.type:error` anywhere in the raw query does not mean the query selects only errors. For example, `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both pass this check. For allowlisted projects on Discover, these requests are consequently rewritten to aggregate `sample_weight` even though they select transactions, which this helper explicitly says do not have that field. This can produce incorrect counts or query failures. Determine eligibility from parsed query constraints rather than a substring.

Top-event selection still uses the unweighted count

Only `timeseries_columns` is transformed for top-events requests; `selected_columns` and `orderby` still come directly from the original request. A request selecting and ordering by `count()` therefore chooses its top groups by stored event count, then displays their weighted counts. With different client sample rates, a group with fewer stored events can have the largest upsampled count and still be omitted from the chart. Apply consistent weighted aggregation to the top-group selection and ordering as well as the returned time series.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New table visualization discards the query results

When the organization has `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled, every dashboard table is rendered with empty columns, empty rows, and empty metadata instead of the fetched `result`. Consequently, populated widgets appear empty regardless of their query results. Pass the actual result data and corresponding columns/metadata to the new visualization before enabling this branch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
Attribute cache key no longer distinguishes organizations

The new React Query key contains only query options, although the query function requests an organization-specific endpoint. With identical filters (for example, all projects and the default date range), switching organizations reuses the previous organization's cached attribute collection and can also share an in-flight request. Include the organization slug in the query key so attribute suggestions cannot come from a different organization.

Normalize error and recording timestamps before merging

Error timestamps fetched from nodestore are Unix seconds, whereas raw rrweb recording event timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Comparing them directly makes errors appear earlier than all recording events, so errors occurring midway through a replay are emitted at the beginning of the summary input rather than alongside the relevant breadcrumbs. Normalize the recording timestamp to seconds (or the error timestamp to milliseconds) before comparing. The new tests use seconds for recording timestamps and therefore do not exercise the production format.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Consume backup codes atomically to enforce single use

Backup codes are read from the user record, checked in memory, and then overwritten with an unconditional update by user ID. Two concurrent login requests can both read the same unused code and both authenticate successfully. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a code already consumed by the other request. Use an atomic conditional update (checking the previously stored value and rejecting or retrying on conflict) or transactional locking so that successful authentication guarantees the code was consumed exactly once.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code authentication can bypass password verification

The existing password check runs only when credentials.totpCode is falsy, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence over TOTP validation. A caller can submit a valid backupCode together with any nonempty totpCode and an incorrect or missing password: password verification is skipped and the arbitrary TOTP is never checked. This allows possession of a backup code alone to authenticate a password-based account. Ensure the required primary credential is verified independently of which second-factor branch is selected.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guard the missing destination before checking its integration

When a Google Meet event has no destination calendar, destructuring the empty array leaves mainHostDestinationCalendar undefined. Reading its integration throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. Booking creation therefore fails for Google Meet event types whose calendar was disconnected or is otherwise unset.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Select the destination belonging to the current credential

EventManager now calls this service separately for every collective host but passes the entire destinationCalendar array each time. This service always uses the first host's calendar ID with the current host's access token. Secondary Office 365 hosts (including those paired with a Google organizer) therefore attempt to write to another account's calendar and fail rather than receiving an event. LarkCalendarService and BaseCalendarService have the same first-element selection problem; these services need credential-specific destination selection as Google now has.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not invert organization slug assignment

The previous code assigned the organization slug when team billing was disabled and stored only requestedSlug when billing was enabled. This change reverses the slug condition: billing-disabled installations now create organizations without a slug, while billing-enabled installations assign the requested slug immediately rather than deferring it. This unrelated change breaks organization URL provisioning and should retain the original condition.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel recurring events using each reference's credential

The new outer loop resolves each collective host's credential, but the allRemainingBookings branch ignores that credential and loops only over the booking owner's credentials, selecting only the first calendar reference of each occurrence. Consequently cancelling an entire collective recurring series leaves secondary hosts' calendar events intact, despite marking all bookings cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's references and delete each with its matching credential.

Initialize destinations before adding collective co-host calendars

If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then silently drops all teamDestinationCalendars, even when other collective hosts have connected calendars. Those hosts receive no directly created calendar events. Initialize an empty array or assign the collected destinations instead of skipping the append.

Preserve the credential ID on video references

The reference builder now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, discarding the credential ID returned by createMeeting. The cancellation handler only deletes video meetings when their reference has a credentialId, so newly created Zoom and other dedicated video meetings will no longer be deleted when their booking is cancelled. Retain result.credentialId for video results.

Restore the destination fallback for references without a calendar ID

When externalCalendarId is null or absent, the new fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that absent value, so it cannot select a configured calendar. Google updates then receive an undefined calendarId and fail. The analogous deletion fallback defaults to primary, leaving events on non-primary calendars undeleted while treating Google's 404 as success. This affects existing references without externalCalendarId, including the credential-less destination creation branch that still does not populate result.externalId.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not replace omitted refresh tokens with a placeholder

This helper injects the literal string "refresh_token" whenever a response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly allows refresh_token to be omitted and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials, so this now overwrites the real stored refresh token with an unusable placeholder. The following refresh fails and the user must reconnect. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Computed Zod keys do not validate or preserve expiry fields

Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces a literal property name (normally "[object Object]"), not a wildcard for response properties. Both computed keys therefore collide, and this z.object also strips unrecognized properties such as expires_in, expiry_date and refresh_token. With credential sharing enabled, valid refresh responses lose their expiry and refresh token; Zoom then computes a NaN expiry and other integrations cannot persist usable refreshed credentials. Use explicit supported fields or a passthrough schema with appropriate validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Persist parsed Google credentials rather than the safeParse result

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result envelope, { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous schema.parse returned the credential object itself. Writing this result directly to credential.key stores the envelope instead of access_token, refresh_token and expiry_date at the top level. The next GoogleCalendarService construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse, breaking calendar access after a refresh even with syncing disabled. Store the result's data.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize sync responses to the contracts expected by SDK callers

The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but several callers still expect the result of their original refresh function: Google and both Zoho integrations read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly from a decoded SDK object. A native Response has none of those properties, regardless of its JSON body, so enabling syncing makes these refreshes throw or store invalid tokens. Decode and adapt the sync response for these callers, or change them to consume a consistent response contract.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize sync responses to the contracts expected by SDK callers

The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but several callers still expect the result of their original refresh function: Google and both Zoho integrations read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly from a decoded SDK object. A native Response has none of those properties, regardless of its JSON body, so enabling syncing makes these refreshes throw or store invalid tokens. Decode and adapt the sync response for these callers, or change them to consume a consistent response contract.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint

The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is a Cal.com user ID, but this call passes credentialId. Consequently the external endpoint receives a credential table primary key as calcomUserId instead of the owner's ID. Since those IDs are unrelated, it can fail to find the account or return another user's credentials when the numbers coincide. Carry credential.userId through the refresh method and pass that value; team credentials should retain the null-user fallback.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce refresh

The new refresh path calls prisma.credential.update, but this module does not import or declare prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws ReferenceError on every Salesforce client initialization. Import the Prisma client used by the other integration services.

Send the Zoom app slug rather than its integration directory name

The refresh request sends appSlug: "zoomvideo", but Zoom credentials are registered with appId "zoom" and the OAuth callback also uses the slug "zoom". An external app store routing refreshes by the supplied appSlug cannot match this request to the Zoom app, preventing refreshes for synced Zoom credentials. Send "zoom" consistently.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but incoming guest addresses are compared without normalization. An address such as Blocked@example.com passes validation and bypasses a blacklist entry of blocked@example.com, allowing invitations to addresses explicitly configured as blocked. Normalize incoming addresses before performing this comparison.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use OR for team admin/owner authorization

The team permission check requires the caller to be both a team admin and a team owner. These are alternative membership roles, so a team admin or owner who is not also the booking organizer or an attendee is rejected with FORBIDDEN. Combine the checks with OR so either authorized role can add guests.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Deduplicate guests on the server before inserting attendees

The variable uniqueGuests only filters addresses already in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the request. The server schema accepts duplicate addresses, so a direct request containing the same new email twice sends both entries to createMany, resulting in duplicate attendee records or an insertion failure if uniqueness is enforced. The dialog's client-side refinement does not protect the API; enforce uniqueness on the server.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Honor event-type email suppression when sending guest updates

sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails and accepts no event-type metadata. Other booking notification paths honor disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding guests consequently sends standard notifications even for event types explicitly configured to suppress them, potentially duplicating custom workflow notifications. Pass the event-type metadata through and apply the same suppression checks.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Update the calendar using the booking organizer's credentials

The handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the caller and the caller's credentials. The booking's calendar references belong to the organizer, not necessarily the caller. When an attendee adds guests, the organizer's calendar event therefore cannot be reliably updated, even though the new attendees have already been persisted. Load the booking owner's credentials and use that owner for the calendar update.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment retryCount atomically instead of writing a stale value

Both failure paths set retryCount to the value fetched at the beginning of the cron run plus one. If two cron requests overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder, they read the same count and overwrite each other, so two failures are recorded as only one. This allows reminders to exceed the intended two-failure limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not let failure bookkeeping abort the remaining reminder batch

The new workflowReminder.update inside the catch block can itself throw and is not protected. For example, if a reminder is deleted after findMany (by a concurrent cleanup run or workflow deletion), scheduling or the success update can fail, and this catch then attempts to update a nonexistent row. Prisma throws, terminating the handler and leaving every remaining reminder in the batch unprocessed. Previously the catch logged the error and continued. Make the retry update tolerate deleted rows and preserve per-reminder error isolation.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve or migrate the removed findMany API

The exported InsightsBookingService no longer exposes findMany; it now only returns SQL fragments through getBaseConditions. Existing callers of findMany will fail type checking (or throw at runtime), and callers using the previous WhereInput-returning condition methods cannot pass the new Sql objects to Prisma model queries. This PR updates only the integration test, not production consumers. Migrate all consumers to parameterized $queryRaw queries in the same change, or retain a compatible querying API until that migration is complete.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendar queries after deleting cache

The cache deletion success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback and never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The wrapper displaying cacheUpdatedAt owns that query but merely forwards props.onChanged, which is optional and does not guarantee a refetch; it also disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Consequently, after a successful deletion the dropdown can continue showing the old cache timestamp and offering deletion of data that no longer exists. Invalidate the connected calendar queries on successful cache deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Await reminder cancellations before completing the request

The cancellation helpers now perform the database deletion or cancelled-flag update, but their promises are discarded inside forEach and are not included in the awaited promises below. Previously the database reminder deletions were explicitly awaited. The handler can therefore return success before cancellation is persisted; in a serverless deployment, execution can stop after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect and await these helper promises, including the equivalent request-reschedule and workflow-update call sites.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel imminent reminders immediately instead of waiting for cron

Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, cancelling a booking five minutes before its reminder is due leaves the email scheduled in SendGrid until after it is sent. The cron also deletes past-due reminder rows before processing cancellations, so it cannot recover this case. Reminders close to their send time need immediate provider cancellation.

Keep immediate cancellations recoverable when SendGrid rejects them

The immediateDelete path still submits cancellations arbitrarily far ahead of the send date, which consumes the same 100 pending-cancellation slots described in this PR. handleNewBooking uses this path for every reschedule. If SendGrid rejects a cancellation because that limit is reached, the error is swallowed and the reminder is never marked cancelled, so cron will not retry it and the old booking's email will still be sent. Workflow and step deletion also use this path and then cascade-delete the reminder rows, losing any retry opportunity.

Persist successful cancellations before another request can fail

The Prisma delete promises accumulated in the loop are lazy and execute only at Promise.all after every SendGrid cancellation succeeds. If any provider request fails, control jumps to the outer catch and none of the earlier successfully cancelled reminders are deleted. On subsequent runs those batches are submitted again; an already-cancelled batch can itself be rejected by SendGrid, repeatedly aborting processing before later reminders are reached. Handle failures per reminder and persist each successful cancellation independently so one failed batch cannot block all remaining cancellations.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Defer import execution until an app is requested

Every import() in this object executes as soon as the app-store index is loaded, so accessing a single calendar or payment provider still starts loading and evaluating all app packages. This splits the modules into chunks but does not defer unused apps, retaining the all-app initialization cost on cold starts. Store loader functions instead and invoke only the selected loader at the call sites. This also allows import failures to be handled by the requesting caller rather than leaving rejected promises for unused apps unobserved.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflict checks

When an override exists on the slot's date, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before evaluating busy times. An override defines working availability, not permission to ignore existing bookings or external calendar events. Consequently, personal events and fixed or round-robin hosts with an override can expose slots that overlap their existing bookings. Continue to the busy-time checks after validating the override.

Multiple override intervals reject slots inside a valid interval

dateOverrides.find searches for any interval that excludes the slot, rather than an interval that contains it. If a host has overrides of 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00 on the same date, a 10:00 slot is rejected by the afternoon interval and a 15:00 slot by the morning interval. Split date-override availability can therefore lose all its slots. Group overrides by date and accept containment in any of that date's intervals.

Override validation checks overlap instead of full slot containment

The new override checks reject only slots ending at or before the override start or starting after its end. For a fixed host available from 10:00 to 11:00, a round-robin slot from 09:30 to 10:30 or 10:30 to 11:30 therefore passes, even though the host is unavailable for part of the meeting. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes. Require the entire slot to fit within an override interval.

Timezone conversion discards midnight rollover

The converted override boundaries retain only hour and minute, discarding their date. For example, a UTC override from 22:00 to 23:00 viewed in UTC+01:30 becomes startTime 1410 and endTime 30. buildSlots discards that range because start is greater than end, so the valid 23:30–00:30 availability disappears. Converted overrides that cross an attendee's midnight need to be split across the corresponding attendee dates rather than reduced to a single minute-of-day range.

Working-hours validation rejects ordinary split schedules

The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it is outside any working-hours interval on that weekday. For a normal schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, morning slots fail against the afternoon interval and afternoon slots fail against the morning interval. Because every host now goes through this check, this removes valid slots even on dates without overrides. Validate that the full slot is contained in at least one applicable interval instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle integrations that lack sender metadata

The new verification unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"], but build_integration() only adds sender when it is present in pipeline state; the updated basic-flow test explicitly creates an integration without this field. If an integration created through that path remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, attempting to install it again raises KeyError and returns a server error instead of the intended invalid-installation response. Handle absent sender information explicitly and fail closed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

false_positives.candidate:
Do not bypass installer verification when the integration row is missing

When no Integration row exists for the supplied installation ID, this branch advances directly to completion without comparing the authenticated GitHub user with the installer. Completion can fetch the installation using the app's credentials in build_integration(), so authenticating as any GitHub user is sufficient to claim such an installation. This also creates a bypass window before the installation webhook has created the row. Missing installer information must fail closed or be verified through another trusted source rather than skipping the new security check.

true_positives.golden_comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Evaluate the queued timestamp for each AssignmentSource instance

`timezone.now()` is evaluated when this module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value receives the same process-start timestamp, rather than the time of its assignment. In long-running webhook workers, the serialized context therefore reports an incorrect queue time for every subsequent change. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to generate the timestamp per instance.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.

true_positives.golden_comment: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated

Changing MetricAlertDetectorHandler to inherit from StatefulDetectorHandler while leaving its body empty leaves counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data abstract. Accessing detector.detector_handler for the registered metric_alert_fire type therefore raises TypeError instead of returning the previous no-op handler. process_detectors does not catch this exception, so processing a detector of this type aborts the batch. true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Spawned workers do not pass the multiprocessing.Process type check

Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which creates SpawnProcess instances. These are not instances of the top-level multiprocessing.Process class, so this check skips kill() for every production worker. When a worker hangs, the manager starts a replacement without stopping the original; the original can subsequently resume flushing the same shards, causing concurrent processing and duplicate production. The identical check in join() also skips termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from the spawn-context process type.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Terminate all remaining workers when the join deadline expires

When the shared join deadline expires, this loop breaks before stopping the current worker or any subsequent workers. This also happens if next_step.join(timeout) consumes the entire timeout. A worker blocked in Redis or Kafka therefore remains alive after the strategy is discarded during rebalancing, and may later resume flushing shards now owned by another consumer. Even after correcting the process type check, this early break still leaks workers. The deadline should limit waiting, not skip termination of the remaining processes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
The magic number 50 for max_wait is used repeatedly throughout the tests. Consider extracting this as a named constant to improve maintainability.

false_positives.candidate:
Bound queued work and apply backpressure

Each work queue is created with no maximum size, and submit always accepts more messages without raising MessageRejected. If processing is slower than Kafka ingestion, or a worker stalls, the consumer continues retaining decoded results and original messages indefinitely. The offset tracker also retains all later offsets behind unfinished work. This can exhaust consumer memory under exactly the slow-item workload this mode is intended to handle; queued and in-flight work need a bound with backpressure.

Create a fresh queue pool for each partition assignment

The factory creates its queue pool only once and passes that same pool to every strategy. Closing or joining a strategy shuts down that pool's workers and queues, but a Kafka rebalance subsequently calls create_with_partitions on the same factory and receives another strategy backed by the stopped pool. New messages then either accumulate without workers or fail to enqueue and are marked completed by submit's exception handler, allowing unprocessed results to be committed. Allocate assignment-scoped workers and offset tracking when creating each strategy.

Drain accepted work before stopping workers and committing final offsets

Graceful shutdown sets every worker's shutdown flag before shutting down the queues. Workers therefore exit after their current item instead of draining queued items, despite shutdown(immediate=False). In addition, strategy.close stops the commit thread before waiting for workers, so results completed during shutdown never receive a final commit. Normal shutdown or partition revocation abandons accepted work and replays already processed results on the next assignment. close/join should drain accepted work (within the supplied timeout) and commit its completed offsets before stopping.

Track delivered offset order rather than requiring consecutive Kafka offsets

The tracker stops at any integer offset absent from all_offsets, even if every delivered message has completed. Kafka can legitimately deliver nonconsecutive offsets, for example when transactional control records or aborted transactions are skipped. If completed offsets 100 and 102 are present in the same commit scan, it commits only 100 even though 102 is safe; with ongoing work after such gaps this unnecessarily retains completed offsets and increases replay and memory usage. Determine the safe prefix of delivered offsets, stopping at outstanding work rather than at offsets Kafka never delivered.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Encode denial-cache components without ambiguous separators

Concatenating resource name and parent folder with underscores produces collisions when either identifier contains underscores. For the same namespace, user and action, name=a_b with parent=c produces the same key as name=a with parent=b_c. A denial for one resource therefore incorrectly denies access to the other, even if its permissions allow access, because Check returns immediately on a denial-cache hit. Use an unambiguous encoding of the components, such as a serialized tuple or length-prefixed values.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

false_positives.candidate:
Include identity type in the denial-cache key

The denial key uses only the parsed subject ID and omits IdentityType, even though permissions differ by identity type. For example, a denied dashboards:read check for anonymous:0 caches a denial that also matches render:0 for the same namespace, dashboard and folder. The renderer is explicitly granted wildcard read permission, but the early cache return now denies it without evaluating those permissions for 30 seconds. Include the identity type (or full subject) in the key to isolate these identities.

true_positives.golden_comment: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. false_positives.candidate:
Preserve federated-group immutability in the CombinedRule hook

useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), but now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated to false. Existing CombinedRule consumers therefore treat Mimir groups with source_tenants as ordinary editable groups and enable Update/Delete for users with external write permission. This removes the explicit protection against modifying federated rules through flows that do not support federation. Preserve the group-level federation check when adapting the legacy hook.

Removing rulerRule also removes Pause and Delete actions

This list item now passes only promRule to RuleActionsButtons. Although AlertRuleMenu computes pause and delete abilities from promRule, its Pause item still requires a Grafana rulerRule and its Delete item still requires rulerRule to exist. Consequently authorized users can no longer pause, resume, or delete rules from either the grouped or filtered Grafana list. These actions need an identifier-based flow or on-demand ruler loading rather than silently disappearing.

skipToken does not actually disable Grafana abilities

Passing skipToken converts the rule to undefined but still returns the abilities computed by useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. For an undefined rule, loading is false, duplicateSupported is true, and Duplicate is allowed whenever the user has Grafana rule-create permission. AlertRuleMenu calls this hook with skipToken for datasource rules and ORs its result with the datasource abilities. true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Device count and admission are not atomic

CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active devices in one database session and inserts the new device in a separate session without any serialization. When the count is one below the configured limit, multiple requests with distinct device IDs can all observe the available slot and each insert successfully, exceeding the limit. This also occurs across Grafana replicas sharing the database, so a process-local lock alone would not fix it. Serialize the count-and-admission operation at the database level and test simultaneous admissions at the limit.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted

TagDevice now propagates the device-limit error to authentication, but tagDeviceUI still inserts the device ID into its 29-minute local cache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When a new device is rejected because the limit is full, that cache entry remains. A second request with the same device ID hits the cache, returns nil without checking the store, and authenticates successfully. Concurrent requests can likewise use the entry before the first admission check finishes. Cache only successful admissions and ensure requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful; add a test that retries a rejected device.

SQLite ID-list construction is quadratic in batch size

Each iteration formats and copies the entire accumulated ID string. false_negatives.golden_comment: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

false_positives.candidate:
Detach asynchronous writes from request cancellation

The legacy-write timeout is derived from the incoming request context, which is canceled when the HTTP handler returns. Since Create now returns without waiting for the goroutine, the legacy operation can receive an already-canceled context or be canceled midway through its write, regardless of the ten-second timeout. The same issue affects Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection. Preserve context values but detach request cancellation before applying the background-write timeout.

Preserve operation ordering for background replication

Each successful mutation launches an independent goroutine with no ordering between writes to the same resource. For example, a client can create a resource and then delete it after Create returns, while the legacy delete executes before the legacy create; the delete fails with not-found and the later create leaves a deleted resource in legacy permanently. Successive updates can likewise overwrite newer legacy data with older data. Serialize or queue replication per resource so the legacy safety copy follows committed operation order.

Replicate the committed update rather than reapplying UpdatedObjectInfo

Legacy.Update now receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the wrapper containing the object committed to unified storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can compute a patch or server-side apply against the old object supplied by each store; if legacy is behind, reapplying it there can produce a different object or fail despite a successful unified update. The previous implementation explicitly passed the unified result to legacy. Replicate a snapshot of res rather than evaluating the original update against legacy state again.

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Recheck the production cache after acquiring the write lock

Concurrent requests arriving before the cache is populated can all read a nil cache and then queue for the write lock. Each queued request subsequently reloads and parses the manifest even though the first request has already populated the cache, serializing redundant disk I/O and delaying requests during cold start. A later reload failure can also replace the successfully populated cache with nil and return an avoidable error. After acquiring the write lock, check the cache again and return it when running outside development mode.

true_positives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Recheck the production cache after acquiring the write lock

Concurrent requests arriving before the cache is populated can all read a nil cache and then queue for the write lock. Each queued request subsequently reloads and parses the manifest even though the first request has already populated the cache, serializing redundant disk I/O and delaying requests during cold start. A later reload failure can also replace the successfully populated cache with nil and return an avoidable error.
